2027-03-24.title: Seventh Wednesday of the Great Fast · Wednesday of Hasha Week
2027-03-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The new covenant sealed in blood
The Son of Man must be lifted up
2027-03-24.alt: Hasha Week (Holy Week), the last week of the Great Fast. Tomorrow is Pesaha: homes prepare the Pesaha appam and paal, and the parish prepares the one Qurbana of the Lord's Supper. In some traditions this day is called Spy Wednesday, recalling the bargain of Judas (Matthew 26:14–16).
2027-03-24.verse: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
theo: Joseph is now in an Egyptian prison, and two of Pharaoh's officers are thrown in with him: the chief cupbearer and the chief baker. One morning he finds them troubled and asks, “Why are your faces downcast today?” They have dreamed, and no one can explain the dreams. Joseph answers, “Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell them to me.” The cupbearer saw a vine with three branches; it budded, blossomed and ripened, and “Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand.” The baker saw three baskets of bread on his head, and birds eating from the top one. “The three branches are three days,” says Joseph, and within three days the cupbearer will be restored. Then the innocent prisoner adds a plea that goes to the heart: “But remember me when it is well with you; please do me the kindness to make mention of me to Pharaoh, and so get me out of this place.” “For in fact I was stolen out of the land of the Hebrews; and here also I have done nothing that they should have put me into the dungeon.” Everything happens as Joseph said, on the third day, and then comes the saddest line of the chapter: “Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.” On the eve of Pesaha the Church sets before us a cup of wine, baskets of bread, an innocent man in chains, three days, and a plea to be remembered. On Friday a condemned man will say to Jesus, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom” (Luke 23:42), and Jesus will not forget him. Tomorrow evening Jesus will take bread and the cup and say, “Do this in remembrance of me” (1 Corinthians 11:24). We are often the forgetful cupbearer; the Holy Qurbana is the place where we learn to remember, and where God remembers us. In Kerala homes this is the day of preparation: rice flour and coconut for the Pesaha appam, jaggery and coconut milk for the paal, and the little palm cross from Hosanna Sunday made ready.

In the second reading Joshua, old and near death, calls all Israel together for his farewell: “I am now old and well advanced in years; and you have seen all that the LORD your God has done to all these nations for your sake, for it is the LORD your God who has fought for you.” He asks one thing: “Therefore be very steadfast to observe and do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, turning aside from it neither to the right nor to the left”, and “hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.” His last word sums up the whole law: “Be very careful, therefore, to love the LORD your God.” Tomorrow Jesus will give his own farewell at the supper table, and his commandment will be the same, made new: love one another as I have loved you. The Epistle explains what Jesus will do with the cup. Christ “is the mediator of a new covenant”, and a covenant, like a will, takes effect through a death. “Hence not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.” Moses sprinkled the people and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that God has ordained for you.” Christ did not enter a sanctuary made by human hands, “but he entered into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf.” And he did not need to do it again and again: “he has appeared once for all at the end of the age to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself.” This is why the Church teaches that the Holy Qurbana is not a new or repeated sacrifice, but the one sacrifice of the Cross made present on our altars (Catechism 1366–1367). The letter ends with hope: Christ “will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.”

The Gospel lets us hear the Lord's heart on the eve of his Passion. “Now my soul is troubled.” John has no scene in the garden like the other Gospels; this is his Gethsemane. Jesus does not pretend to feel no fear. Yet he does not ask to be spared: “it is for this reason that I have come to this hour. Father, glorify your name.” A voice answers from heaven, “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.” Some say it thundered; others say an angel spoke. Jesus tells them, “Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be driven out. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.” John adds: “He said this to indicate the kind of death he was to die.” The Cross is a throne, a magnet, a light raised on a hill. The St Thomas Christians have kept for centuries a cross of their own, the Mar Thoma Sliva, carved without a figure, its arms blossoming, a dove descending upon it: the Cross seen already in the light of the Resurrection. Many still call this day Spy Wednesday, remembering that Judas went to the chief priests and asked, “What will you give me if I betray him to you?” (Matthew 26:15). Judas is not someone else's story. Each of us can sell the Lord for small things. But the One who will be lifted up draws all people to himself, even those who betrayed him, if they will only turn and look.
conn: The cupbearer's cup and the baker's bread stand beside the innocent Joseph; the Fathers saw in them a faint sketch of the bread and the cup that Christ would give before his Passion.
Joseph pleads to be remembered (Genesis 40:14); the thief on the cross asks the same of Jesus (Luke 23:42); and Jesus says at the Supper, Do this in remembrance of me (Luke 22:19).
The cupbearer is restored on the third day (Genesis 40:20); Hosea foresees that on the third day God will raise us up (Hosea 6:2); Christ was raised on the third day (1 Corinthians 15:4).
Joshua's farewell (Joshua 23–24) and Jesus' farewell discourse at the Last Supper (John 13–17) both end in a call to love and hold fast.
Moses' words at Sinai (Exodus 24:8) are repeated in Hebrews 9:20 and fulfilled when Jesus says, This is my blood of the covenant (Matthew 26:28).
Moses lifted up the bronze serpent (Numbers 21:8–9); Jesus says the Son of Man must be lifted up (John 3:14); Isaiah's servant shall be exalted and lifted up (Isaiah 52:13).
outline: Ask: whom have I forgotten, and do I believe that God remembers me?
The cupbearer who forgot and the Lord who remembers.
Point 2 · Be very careful to love
The blood of the new covenant, made present at the altar.
Point 4 · When I am lifted up
The Cross that draws all people.
“And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”
live: Prepare the Pesaha appam and paal together as a family, with the palm cross from Hosanna Sunday, and pray while you work.
Call or visit someone who once helped you and whom you have not thanked.
Spend five quiet minutes before a crucifix or the Mar Thoma Sliva tonight.
Make a last good confession before Pesaha, if you have not yet done so.
fathers: Joseph asked the cupbearer to remember him, and was forgotten for two whole years. The thief asked Christ to remember him, and that very day he was in paradise. People forget those who did them good; Christ remembers even the sinner who turns to him at the last hour.
He stretched out his hands on the Cross to embrace the ends of the earth. Lifted up on Golgotha, the centre of the world, he draws all peoples to himself.
magis: The Eucharist is a sacrifice because it re-presents, makes present, the sacrifice of the Cross, and applies its fruit.
The sacrifice of Christ and the sacrifice of the Eucharist are one single sacrifice; only the manner of offering is different.
Being lifted up on the Cross signifies and announces his lifting up by the Ascension into heaven.
The Paschal mystery of Christ cannot remain only in the past: it is made present in the liturgy.
2027-03-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, innocent one in chains, you did not forget the thief who begged to be remembered. Forgive us when we forget you and those who did us good. Mediator of the new covenant, you offered yourself once for all; make us worthy to stand at your altar tomorrow, where your one sacrifice is made present. Lifted up on the Cross, draw us and all people to yourself, and keep us faithful in love as Joshua taught his people. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Joseph asked the cupbearer to remember him and was forgotten. At the Holy Qurbana Christ says, Do this in remembrance of me, and the Church never forgets: she makes his one sacrifice present until he comes.
The cup that the cupbearer placed in Pharaoh's hand was only wine; the cup the priest lifts at the altar is the blood of the new covenant.

quick: In prison Joseph interprets the dreams of the cupbearer and the baker, and begs to be remembered; he is forgotten.
Christ, mediator of the new covenant, offered himself once for all; the Qurbana makes that one sacrifice present.
Troubled in soul, Jesus says: when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself.
2027-03-24.action: Prepare the Pesaha appam and paal together, and thank one person you have forgotten.
2027-03-24.question: Whom have I forgotten, and have I forgotten that the Lord remembers me?
term: The St Thomas Cross: the ancient cross of the St Thomas Christians, without a corpus, with blossoming arms and a dove above it, proclaiming the victory of the Cross and the gift of the Spirit.

family.explain: Joseph was in prison, though he had done nothing wrong. The king's cupbearer had a dream, and Joseph explained it: in three days you will be free. Joseph asked him: please remember me! But the cupbearer forgot. Jesus never forgets anyone. On the Cross a man asked him, Jesus, remember me, and Jesus promised him heaven that same day.
family.intention: We pray for prisoners, especially those who are innocent, and for everyone who feels forgotten.
family.ask: Ask: “Who has been kind to us whom we have forgotten to thank?”

illus: A young engineer from Changanassery had studied with the help of a scholarship arranged by an old schoolteacher in his parish. He promised to visit her when he got his first job, and then, busy and far away, he forgot. On the Wednesday of Holy Week, home for Pesaha, he heard the reading at Qurbana: the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him. That evening he went to her house with a packet of sweets. She was bedridden now, and she said she had prayed for him every night. On Pesaha night she ate the first piece of appam from his hand.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you remember us even when we forget you. Draw us to yourself now as we pray. Amen.
share: But remember me when it is well with you (Genesis 40:14). Whom have I forgotten now that things are well with me?
Be very careful, therefore, to love the LORD your God (Joshua 23:11). Where has my love for God grown careless?
he has appeared once for all to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself (Hebrews 9:26). How do I prepare to take part in that one sacrifice at the Qurbana?
when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself (John 12:32). What draws me to the Cross, and what holds me back?
pm.resp: Lord, remember us in your kingdom.
interc: For the Church, that she may faithfully celebrate the memorial of the Lord's Passion.
For prisoners, especially the innocent and the forgotten.
For all who are preparing the Pesaha in their homes and parishes.
For those tempted, like Judas, to sell their faith for small gain.
For our group, that we may never forget the Lord who remembers us.
pm.close: Father, your Son was lifted up on the Cross to draw all people to himself, and he never forgets those who call on him. Keep us faithful in love, prepare our hearts for his Supper, and remember us in your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Joseph is in prison, though he has done nothing wrong. He explains the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker: a cup of wine, baskets of bread, three days. And he begs the cupbearer: remember me when it is well with you (Genesis 40:14).

But the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him (Genesis 40:23). How often we are like him: we forget those who helped us, and we forget God when things go well. On Friday a dying man will say, Jesus, remember me, and Jesus will not forget.
Old Joshua tells Israel: be very careful, therefore, to love the LORD your God (Joshua 23:11). Tomorrow Jesus will give his farewell at the supper table, and his commandment too will be love.

Hebrews says that Christ has appeared once for all to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself (Hebrews 9:26). The Holy Qurbana does not repeat that sacrifice; it makes the one sacrifice of the Cross present for us. Let us come to it tomorrow with clean hearts.

In the Gospel Jesus says: now my soul is troubled. But he does not run from the hour: Father, glorify your name. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself (John 12:32). Tonight, as we prepare the Pesaha appam, let us look at the Cross and let him draw us. Amen.
kids: Children, Joseph asked a man in prison: please remember me! But the man forgot. Jesus never forgets us! Tonight, can you help prepare the Pesaha appam, and say thank you to someone you forgot to thank?

intro: Theme: “And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”
The forgotten prisoner and the Lord who remembers, Joshua's farewell, the blood of the new covenant offered once for all, and the Son of Man lifted up.

sub: A cup, bread and three days.
q: But remember me when it is well with you; please do me the kindness to make mention of me to Pharaoh, and so get me out of this place.
Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”
points.apply: Thank one person you have forgotten, and ask the Lord to remember you in his kingdom.

q: Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, “See the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
But as it is, he has appeared once for all at the end of the age to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Pesaha, so that you may share worthily in the one sacrifice.

q: See, my servant shall prosper; he shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
points.apply: Spend five quiet minutes tonight before a crucifix and let the Lord draw you.

concl: We forget, but the Lord remembers; we fail, but his one sacrifice stands for ever.
Lifted up on the Cross, he draws all people to himself; tomorrow he will give himself into our hands.
2027-03-24.resolve: Prepare the Pesaha table, make your confession, and thank one forgotten benefactor.
